title: Concurrent token-surge sculptor for SSE/WebSocket streaming benchmarks
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Build a high-fidelity, programmable load harness (the 'sculptor') that can generate realistic streaming chat/completions traffic over both Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket protocols. The sculptor should model token-level emission, prefix/KV-cache warm and cold scenarios, multi-tenant mixes, connection churn, client multiplexing, and backpressure to accurately measure tokens/sec, p95 chunk latency, and end-to-end tail behaviors at scale. Outputs feed into regression detectors and can gate releases via configurable SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Driver can simulate 50k concurrent sessions across SSE and WebSocket with configurable client mixes
Per-session token emission matches user-configurable distributions (burst, steady, ramp) and supports sampling of real production traces
Collects and exports per-tenant and global metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 chunk latency, connection establish/fail rates, and KV-cache hit/miss breakdown
Automated regression detector compares current run to baseline and raises alerts when p95 increases by >10% or tokens/sec drops by >8%
Fault injection hooks: network latency, packet loss, abrupt disconnects, and model fallback transitions
SSE and WebSocket implementations exercised with both streaming-chunk and chunked-json payloads and validated against server compatibility failures
Dashboard (Grafana) and CI gate integration (buildkite/job) available; end-to-end run reproducible via single CLI invocation
technical_notes: We will implement a modular client model: Transport -> SessionBehavior -> TokenEmitter. Transport supports SSE/WS and an abstracted test socket for instrumentation.

TokenEmitter will support parametric distributions (Poisson, Pareto, custom trace replay). We prefer probabilistic sampling for diversity but include deterministic trace replay for regression reproducibility.

To reduce infra cost during large runs, we’ll use connection multiplexing (N logical sessions per physical TCP/WS connection) while preserving independent KV-cache entropy by tagging requests with session IDs and optionally shimmed connection-scoped cache behavior.
Metrics ingestion via StatsD/OTLP with client-side histograms to avoid scraping blind spots. We will emit per-request trace context for p95 attribution in Jaeger.

Regression detector implements two modes: 'quick' (statistical snapshot comparison) and 'deep' (time-series anomaly detection over multiple runs using rolling baselines). Quick mode used in CI; deep mode for nightly sweeps.
Keep cost vs fidelity trade-offs explicit: high-fidelity parameterization increases agent complexity and run cost; provide prebuilt presets (smoke, hourly, full-scale) to control scope.
Security: no customer PII in synthetic traces; when using masked replay of production traces, require RBAC and audit log ACLs.
implementation_steps: Design API for sculptor: CLI + YAML profile descriptors (client_mix, token_distribution, kvcache_profile, fault_schedule)
Prototyping: implement Transport abstraction and basic SSE/WS clients with single-session token emission
Add TokenEmitter distributions and trace-replay adapter; validate against small local model serving instance
Scale: implement connection multiplexing layer and multi-process coordinator for horizontal scaling
Metrics: integrate OTLP exporter and per-session histogram buckets; wire into existing Grafana dashboards
Regression: build quick comparator and CI hook; create baseline storage for nightly deep runs
Runbook: add docs, example profiles (realistic-chat, bursty-bots, low-latency-seek) and troubleshooting guidance
PRs, infra provisioning, and a staged rollout (dev -> qa -> perf-nightly)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Running at full scale is expensive and may consume GPU capacity; Mitigation: provide 'preview' mode that reduces concurrency but preserves relative patterns and use dedicated test cluster nodes
Risk: Connection multiplexing may obscure per-connection failure modes; Mitigation: toggle multiplexing off in certain presets and correlate synthetic session IDs with server logs
Risk: Regression false positives due to non-deterministic models or infra noise; Mitigation: compute confidence intervals, require multiple failed runs before blocking a release
Risk: Overfitting harness to our runtime internals and missing real client behaviors; Mitigation: sample production traces and interview client SDK teams for corner cases
